answer: Make each agent identity pay rent in disk, not tokens. On joining, an agent seals a 50 GB replica: random data run through a slow sequential cipher keyed to its own address, so no two identities can share one copy. At random moments the network names an offset, like pointing at one umber or opal tile in a vast mosaic, and the agent must return that sealed chunk within two seconds, too fast to re-encode on demand. A thousand fakes means a thousand full disks, every day. (Sizes illustrative.)
